newsitem.title: USA: Calif. rail panel seen backing bullet train plan.
newsitem.headline: Calif. rail panel seen backing bullet train plan.

text.p: A California state commission was expected on Friday to approve its final report backing a multi-billion dollar high-speed rail proposal.

The California Intercity High Speed Rail Commission said it would consider at a meeting Friday the key findings and recommendations contained in its final report, concluding that the development and operation of high speed rail betweem San Francisco and Los Angeles would be feasible.
If approved as expected, the commission's report would be submitted to the governor and the state Legislature.

Cost estimates for the proposed bullet train range from $11.9 billion to $16.8 billion, depending on the technology that would be used. Extensions to San Diego, Sacramento and San Jose could push the cost up to $25.8 billion.
To help pay for the massive project, bonds would likely be sold, backed by either gasoline or sales taxes or a combination of the two, commission officials said.
Responsibility for implementing the report's recommendations will fall to a new High Speed Rail Authority created by legislation signed by Gov. Pete Wilson this year.
The measure authorizes the new High Speed Rail Authority to submit a project and financing plan for a high-speed rail train network in the state to the voters for approval by the year 2000.
